suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-18 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited critical review characterizes cyclothymic disorder as a chronic and impairing disorder on the bipolar spectrum, without establishing that any individual with cyclothymic disorder will progress to full bipolar disorder. Require independently established cyclothymic disorder and a separately established full bipolar disorder (type I or II) before presenting the relationship; the cited critical review characterizes cyclothymic disorder as a chronic and impairing disorder on the bipolar spectrum and does not establish that any individual will progress to full bipolar disorder. Preserve major depressive disorder, other bipolar-spectrum presentations, substance use, medications, personality factors, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer bipolar disorder from hypomanic or depressive symptoms alone, and do not treat this spectrum-level association as proof that cyclothymic disorder caused an individual's bipolar disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
